His words: ﴿And We built above you seven strong [heavens]﴾ mean: the seven heavens, in their vastness, height, firmness, and perfection, and their adornment with the fixed stars and the wandering planets. For this reason He said: ﴿And We made a brilliant lamp﴾, meaning the bright sun, which gives light to the entire world, whose radiance shines upon all the people of the earth.

* *

His words: ﴿And We sent down from the rain-bearing clouds water pouring forth﴾. Al-Awfi reported from Ibn Abbas: "﴿al-Mu'sirat﴾ [the rain-bearing ones] are the winds."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id narrated to us, Abu Dawud al-Hafari [in A: "al-Jawni"] narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And We sent down from the al-Mu'sirat﴾, he said: "The winds." Likewise said Ikrimah, Mujahid, Qatadah, Muqatil, al-Kalbi, Zayd ibn Aslam, and his son Abd al-Rahman: "It means the winds." The meaning of this view is that they draw the rain from the clouds.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn Abbas: ﴿from al-Mu'sirat﴾, meaning: from the clouds. Likewise said Ikrimah also, Abu al-Aliyah, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and al-Thawri. Ibn Jarir chose this view.

Al-Farra' said: "They are the clouds which drip with rain but have not yet rained, just as one says of a woman, 'mu'sir', when her menstruation is near but she has not yet menstruated."

It is reported from al-Hasan and Qatadah: ﴿from al-Mu'sirat﴾ means: the heavens. This is a strange view.

The more apparent view is that what is meant by al-Mu'sirat is the clouds, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿It is Allah who sends the winds, so they stir up clouds, and He spreads them across the sky however He wills and breaks them into fragments, and you see the rain emerging from within them﴾ [Ar-Rum: 48], meaning: from between them.

* *

His words: ﴿water pouring forth﴾. Mujahid, Qatadah, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "﴿thajjaj﴾ means: poured down." al-Thawri said: "Consecutive." Ibn Zayd said: "Abundant."

Ibn Jarir said: "The word al-thajj is not known in the Arabic language to describe abundance; rather, al-thajj is the consecutive pouring." From it is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "The best Hajj is al-'ajj and al-thajj," meaning: the pouring of the blood of the sacrificial camels. [This is the statement of Ibn Jarir, Tafsir al-Tabari (30/5). This hadith has come from the narrations of Ibn Umar, Abu Bakr, Jabir, and Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with them. For its takhrij and discussion see Nasb al-Rayah by al-Imam al-Zayla'i (3/33-35).] Thus he said. I say: In the hadith of the mustahadah [woman with irregular bleeding], when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: "I recommend that you use cotton," meaning: that you stuff yourself with cotton, she said: "O Messenger of Allah, it is more than that; I am only pouring forth in a torrent (athujju thajjan)." [This is the hadith of Hamnah bint Jahsh, narrated by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad (6/439), Abu Dawud in al-Sunan no. (287), and al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan no. (128).] This indicates the use of al-thajj for the consecutive, abundant pouring. And Allah knows best.

* *

His words: ﴿That We may bring forth thereby grain and vegetation and gardens of entwined growth﴾. That is: so that by this abundant, pure, beneficial, and blessed water We may bring forth ﴿grain﴾ stored for humans and cattle, ﴿and vegetation﴾, meaning green plants eaten fresh, ﴿and gardens﴾, meaning orchards and gardens of various fruits, different colors, varied tastes and scents, even if they are all in one single place of the earth, gathered together. For this reason He said: ﴿and gardens of entwined growth﴾. Ibn Abbas and others said: ﴿alfafan﴾ means: gathered together. This is like His words: ﴿And on the earth are neighboring tracts and gardens of grapevines and crops and palm trees, [some] multiple from a single root and others not, watered with one water. Yet We cause some of them to exceed others in fruit﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 4], to the end of the verse.

Ibn Kathir said, [may Allah be exalted], informing about the Day of Judgment, which is the Day of Decision (yawm al-fasl), that it is fixed to a known term, which is neither increased nor decreased, and that none knows its exact time except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as He said: ﴿And We do not delay it except for a known term.﴾ [Hud: 104]

﴿The Day the Trumpet is blown, and you will come forth in multitudes.﴾ Mujahid said: "Zumaran" (in groups). Ibn Jarir said: it means every nation comes with its messenger, as in His saying: ﴿The Day We will call every people with their leader.﴾ [al-Isra: 71] [Tafsir al-Tabari (30/60).]

Al-Bukhari said: ﴿The Day the Trumpet is blown, and you will come forth in multitudes.﴾ Muhammad narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Between the two blasts is forty."

They said: "Forty days?" He said: "I refuse (abaytu)." They said: "Forty months?" He said: "I refuse." They said: "Forty years?" He said: "I refuse." He said: "Then Allah will send down water from the sky, and they will sprout as herbs sprout. Nothing of the human being will remain that does not decay, except one bone, which is the coccyx (ajb al-dhanab), and from it the creation will be reassembled on the Day of Resurrection." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4935.]

﴿And the sky will be opened and will become gates.﴾ That is, paths and passages for the descent of the angels. ﴿And the mountains will be moved away and become a mirage.﴾ As in His saying: ﴿And you see the mountains, thinking them fixed, while they pass as the passing of clouds.﴾ [al-Naml: 88], and His saying: ﴿And the mountains will be like carded wool.﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 5]

Here He said: ﴿and become a mirage﴾, meaning that to the observer it appears to be something, yet it is nothing; after this it will vanish completely, leaving neither trace nor sign, as He said: ﴿And they ask you about the mountains; say, my Lord will blow them away with a blast, and leave them a level plain, in which you will see no crookedness or unevenness.﴾ [Ta-Ha: 105-107] And He said: ﴿The Day We set the mountains moving and you see the earth laid bare.﴾ [al-Kahf: 47]

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, Hell has been ever lying in wait﴾, meaning: prepared and readied, ﴿for the transgressors﴾, who are the rebellious, the disobedient who oppose the messengers, ﴿a place of return﴾, meaning: a place of return, a destination, an abode, and a lodging. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed, Hell has been ever lying in wait﴾: it means that no one enters Paradise until he passes by the Fire; if he has a passport he is saved, otherwise he is detained. Sufyan al-Thawri said: "Over it are three bridges (qanatir)."

* *

His saying: ﴿Remaining therein for ages (ahqab)﴾, meaning: abiding therein for ages. Ahqab is the plural of huqb, which is a period of time. Scholars differed about its duration. He said: "We find it to be eighty years, each year twelve months, each month thirty days, each day a thousand years." [Tafsir al-Tabari (30/8).]

Likewise it is narrated from Abu Hurayrah, Abdullah ibn Amr, Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Amr ibn Maymun, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and al-Dahhak. And from al-Hasan and al-Suddi as well: seventy years, similarly. And from Abdullah ibn Amr: the huqb is forty years, each day of which is like a thousand years of what you count. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated both.

Bushayr ibn Ka'b said: It was mentioned to me that one huqb is three hundred years, each year three hundred and sixty days, each day of which is like a thousand years. Ibn Jarir narrated it, and Ibn Abi Hatim.

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned from Umar ibn Ali ibn Abi Bakr al-Asfadhani: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah al-Fazari narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning His saying: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾.

Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Mirdas narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Muslim Abu al-Mu'alla narrated to us, who said: I asked Sulayman al-Taymi: "Does anyone come out of the Fire?" Then he said: Sulayman ibn Muslim is a well-known Basran.

Al-Suddi said: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾: seven hundred huqb, each huqb seventy years, each year three hundred and sixty days, each day like a thousand years of what you count.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: this verse is abrogated by His saying: ﴿So taste; We will increase you only in punishment.﴾

Khalid ibn Ma'dan said: this verse and His saying: ﴿except what your Lord wills﴾ [Hud: 107] concern the people of monotheism. Ibn Jarir narrated both.

Then he said: It is possible that His saying ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾ is connected to His saying ﴿they will taste therein neither coolness nor drink﴾, and then Allah will bring upon them after that a punishment of another kind and another type. Then he said: The correct view is that they have no end, as Qatadah and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said. He had said before this:

Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi narrated to me, Amr ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us, from Zuhayr, from Salim: I heard al-Hasan being asked about His saying: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾. He said: As for the ahqab, there is no number for them except eternal abiding in the Fire; but they mention that the huqb is seventy years, each day of which is like a thousand years of what you count.

Sa'id narrated from Qatadah: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾, which means that which has no cessation; whenever one huqb passes, another huqb comes after it. It was mentioned to us that the huqb is eighty years.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾: no one knows the count of these ahqab except Allah, but one huqb is eighty years, the year is three hundred and sixty days, each day like a thousand years of what you count. Ibn Jarir narrated both. [Tafsir al-Tabari (30/9).]

* *

His saying: ﴿They will not taste therein any coolness or drink﴾, meaning: they will find in Hell no coolness for their hearts, nor any pleasant drink by which to nourish themselves. Hence He said: ﴿except boiling water and dark, pus-like fluid (ghassaq)﴾. Abu al-Aliyah said: He excepted from coolness the hamim (boiling water), and from drink the ghassaq. Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said likewise. As for the hamim, it is the hot water whose heat has reached its extreme. The ghassaq is what has gathered from the pus, sweat, tears and wounds of the people of the Fire; it is cold beyond endurance, and its stench cannot be faced. We have already discussed the ghassaq in the commentary on Surah Sad [verse 57], sufficiently so that it need not be repeated. May Allah protect us from that by His favour and generosity.

Ibn Jarir said: It was also said that the meaning of His saying ﴿they will not taste therein any coolness﴾ is sleep, as al-Kindi said:

"Her cool lips cooled upon me, then turned me away from her, and from her kisses, the coolness..."

meaning by "coolness": drowsiness and sleep. [Tafsir al-Tabari (30/9).] He mentioned it thus without attributing it to anyone. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through al-Suddi from Murrah al-Tayyib, and it was also transmitted from Mujahid. Al-Baghawi related it from Abu Ubaydah and al-Kisa'i as well.

His saying: ﴿a fitting recompense﴾, meaning: this punishment they have come to is in accordance with their corrupt deeds which they used to do in the world. Said by Mujahid, Qatadah, and others.

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, they did not expect a reckoning﴾, meaning: they did not believe that there is an abode in which they would be requited and called to account, ﴿and they denied Our signs with complete denial﴾, meaning: they used to deny the proofs and evidences of Allah upon His creation which He sent down upon His messengers, meeting them with denial and obstinacy.

* *

His saying: ﴿kidhdhaban﴾, meaning: denial (takdhib). It is a verbal noun (masdar) not from the verb itself. They said: a Bedouin was heard asking al-Farra' at al-Marwah: "Is shaving (al-halq) more beloved to you, or shortening (al-qisar)?" Some of them recited the verse:

"How long has it kept me from my companions, and from needs whose fulfilment is my cure..."

* *

His saying: ﴿And We have recorded everything in a Book﴾, meaning: We have known the deeds of all the servants, and recorded them against them, and We will recompense them for that: if good, then good; if evil, then evil.

* *

His saying: ﴿So taste; We will increase you only in punishment﴾, meaning: it will be said to the people of the Fire: taste what you are in; We will increase you only in punishment of its kind, ﴿and of other kinds of similar punishments﴾ [Sad: 58].

Qatadah said, from Abu Ayyub al-Azdi, from Abdullah ibn Amr who said: No verse was revealed concerning the people of the Fire more severe than this: ﴿So taste; We will increase you only in punishment.﴾ He said: They are in increasing punishment forever.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mus'ab al-Suri narrated to us, Khalid ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Jassar ibn Farqad narrated to us, from al-Hasan who said: I asked Abu Barzah al-Aslami about the most severe verse in the Book of Allah for the people of the Fire. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite: ﴿So taste; We will increase you only in punishment﴾, and he said: "The people perished through their disobedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." Here He said: ﴿and become a mirage﴾, meaning that to the observer it appears to be something, yet it is nothing; after this it will vanish completely, leaving neither trace nor sign, as He said: ﴿And they ask you about the mountains; say, my Lord will blow them away with a blast, and leave them a level plain, in which you will see no crookedness or unevenness.﴾ [Ta-Ha: 105-107] And He said: ﴿The Day We set the mountains moving and you see the earth laid bare.﴾ [al-Kahf: 47]

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, Hell has been ever lying in wait﴾, meaning: prepared and readied, ﴿for the transgressors﴾, who are the rebellious, the disobedient who oppose the messengers, ﴿a place of return﴾, meaning: a place of return, a destination, an abode, and a lodging. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed, Hell has been ever lying in wait﴾: it means that no one enters Paradise until he passes by the Fire; if he has a passport he is saved, otherwise he is detained. Sufyan al-Thawri said: "Over it are three bridges (qanatir)."

* *

His saying: ﴿Remaining therein for ages (ahqab)﴾, meaning: abiding therein for ages. Ahqab is the plural of huqb, which is a period of time. Scholars differed about its duration. Ibn Jarir said, from Ibn Humayd, from Mihran, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Ammar al-Dhuhni, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, who said: Ali ibn Abi Talib said to Hilal al-Hajari: "What do you find the huqb to be in the revealed Book of Allah?" He said: "We find it to be eighty years, each year twelve months, each month thirty days, each day a thousand years." [Tafsir al-Tabari (30/8).]

Likewise it is narrated from Abu Hurayrah, Abdullah ibn Amr, Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Amr ibn Maymun, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and al-Dahhak. And from al-Hasan and al-Suddi as well: seventy years, similarly. And from Abdullah ibn Amr: the huqb is forty years, each day of which is like a thousand years of what you count. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated both.

Bushayr ibn Ka'b said: It was mentioned to me that one huqb is three hundred years, each year three hundred and sixty days, each day of which is like a thousand years. Ibn Jarir narrated it, and Ibn Abi Hatim.

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned from Umar ibn Ali ibn Abi Bakr al-Asfadhani: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah al-Fazari narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning His saying: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾.

He said: "The huqb is [a thousand] months, the month is thirty days, the year is twelve months, the year is three hundred and sixty days, each day of which is a thousand years of what you count; so the huqb is thirty million years." [Its narration is also in Ibn Abi Asim's Musnad as cited in al-Busiri's Ithaf al-Mahara, and al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (8/292) through Ya'qub ibn Ka'b, from Marwan, from Ja'far, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, marfu': "One huqb is thirty thousand years."] This is an extremely odd (munkar) hadith, and al-Qasim and his narrator Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr are both abandoned (matruk).

Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Mirdas narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Muslim Abu al-Mu'alla narrated to us, who said: I asked Sulayman al-Taymi: "Does anyone come out of the Fire?" He said: Nafi' narrated to me, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "By Allah, no one will come out of the Fire until he remains therein for ages (ahqab)." He said: "The huqb is some eighty years, and the year is three hundred and sixty days of what you count." [Musnad al-Bazzar no. 2249, Kashf al-Astar; also al-Daylami in Musnad al-Firdaws no. 7029 through Ziyad ibn Abi Ziyad, from Sulayman ibn Muslim, similarly; al-Haythami in al-Majma' (10/395) said: "It contains Sulayman ibn Muslim al-Khashshab, who is extremely weak."]

Then he said: Sulayman ibn Muslim is a well-known Basran.

Al-Suddi said: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾: seven hundred huqb, each huqb seventy years, each year three hundred and sixty days, each day like a thousand years of what you count.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: this verse is abrogated by His saying: ﴿So taste; We will increase you only in punishment.﴾

Khalid ibn Ma'dan said: this verse and His saying: ﴿except what your Lord wills﴾ [Hud: 107] concern the people of monotheism. Ibn Jarir narrated both.

Then he said: It is possible that His saying ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾ is connected to His saying ﴿they will taste therein neither coolness nor drink﴾, and then Allah will bring upon them after that a punishment of another kind and another type. Then he said: The correct view is that they have no end, as Qatadah and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said. He had said before this:

Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi narrated to me, Amr ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us, from Zuhayr, from Salim: I heard al-Hasan being asked about His saying: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾. He said: As for the ahqab, there is no number for them except eternal abiding in the Fire; but they mention that the huqb is seventy years, each day of which is like a thousand years of what you count.

Sa'id narrated from Qatadah: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾, which means that which has no cessation; whenever one huqb passes, another huqb comes after it. It was mentioned to us that the huqb is eighty years.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾: no one knows the count of these ahqab except Allah, but one huqb is eighty years, the year is three hundred and sixty days, each day like a thousand years of what you count. Ibn Jarir narrated both. [Tafsir al-Tabari (30/9).]

* *

His saying: ﴿They will not taste therein any coolness or drink﴾, meaning: they will find in Hell no coolness for their hearts, nor any pleasant drink by which to nourish themselves. Hence He said: ﴿except boiling water and dark, pus-like fluid (ghassaq)﴾. Abu al-Aliyah said: He excepted from coolness the hamim (boiling water), and from drink the ghassaq. Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said likewise. As for the hamim, it is the hot water whose heat has reached its extreme. The ghassaq is what has gathered from the pus, sweat, tears and wounds of the people of the Fire; it is cold beyond endurance, and its stench cannot be faced. We have already discussed the ghassaq in the commentary on Surah Sad [verse 57], sufficiently so that it need not be repeated. May Allah protect us from that by His favour and generosity.

Ibn Jarir said: It was also said that the meaning of His saying ﴿they will not taste therein any coolness﴾ is sleep, as al-Kindi said:

"Her cool lips cooled upon me, then turned me away from her, and from her kisses, the coolness..."

meaning by "coolness": drowsiness and sleep. [Tafsir al-Tabari (30/9).] He mentioned it thus without attributing it to anyone. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through al-Suddi from Murrah al-Tayyib, and it was also transmitted from Mujahid. Al-Baghawi related it from Abu Ubaydah and al-Kisa'i as well.

* *

His saying: ﴿a fitting recompense﴾, meaning: this punishment they have come to is in accordance with their corrupt deeds which they used to do in the world. Said by Mujahid, Qatadah, and others.

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, they did not expect a reckoning﴾, meaning: they did not believe that there is an abode in which they would be requited and called to account, ﴿and they denied Our signs with complete denial﴾, meaning: they used to deny the proofs and evidences of Allah upon His creation which He sent down upon His messengers, meeting them with denial and obstinacy.

* *

His saying: ﴿kidhdhaban﴾, meaning: denial (takdhib). It is a verbal noun (masdar) not from the verb itself. They said: a Bedouin was heard asking al-Farra' at al-Marwah: "Is shaving (al-halq) more beloved to you, or shortening (al-qisar)?" Some of them recited the verse:

"How long has it kept me from my companions, and from needs whose fulfilment is my cure..."

* *

His saying: ﴿And We have recorded everything in a Book﴾, meaning: We have known the deeds of all the servants, and recorded them against them, and We will recompense them for that: if good, then good; if evil, then evil.

* *

His saying: ﴿So taste; We will increase you only in punishment﴾, meaning: it will be said to the people of the Fire: taste what you are in; We will increase you only in punishment of its kind, ﴿and of other kinds of similar punishments﴾ [Sad: 58].

Qatadah said, from Abu Ayyub al-Azdi, from Abdullah ibn Amr who said: No verse was revealed concerning the people of the Fire more severe than this: ﴿So taste; We will increase you only in punishment.﴾ He said: They are in increasing punishment forever.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mus'ab al-Suri narrated to us, Khalid ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Jassar ibn Farqad narrated to us, from al-Hasan who said: I asked Abu Barzah al-Aslami about the most severe verse in the Book of Allah for the people of the Fire. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite: ﴿So taste; We will increase you only in punishment﴾, and he said: "The people perished through their disobedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." [Also narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th no. 635 through Muhammad ibn Ghalib, from Muslim ibn Ibrahim, from Jassar ibn Farqad, as a mawquf report; by Ibn Mardawayh in his Tafsir as cited in al-Zayla'i's Takhrij al-Kashshaf (4/145) through Ja'far ibn Jassar, from his father, from al-Hasan; and by al-Tha'labi in his Tafsir as cited in al-Zayla'i (4/145) through Mahdi ibn Maymun, from al-Hasan ibn Dinar, from al-Hasan, from Abu Barzah, marfu', similarly.]

Jassar ibn Farqad: completely weak in hadith.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said, reporting about the people of happiness and what Allah, the Exalted, has prepared for them of honour and lasting bliss, saying: ﴿Indeed, for the righteous there is a place of success﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and al-Dahhak said: a place of recreation (mutanazzahan). Mujahid and Qatadah said: they achieved success, so they were saved from the Fire. The more apparent view here is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas, because He said after it: ﴿gardens﴾, which are orchards of palm trees and others, ﴿and grapes, and maidens of equal age﴾, meaning and virgin maidens of full bosom (kawa'ib). Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and others said: ﴿kawa'ib﴾ means nawahid (firm-breasted), meaning that their breasts are firm and have not sagged, because they are virgins, ʿurub (loving their husbands), atrab (of one age), i.e., of a single age, as its explanation has preceded in Surah al-Waqi'ah.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Dashtaki narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Abu Sufyan Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Rabb ibn Taym al-Yashkuri, Atiyyah ibn Sulayman Abu al-Ghaith narrated to us, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Qasim ibn Abi al-Qasim al-Dimashqi, from Abu Umamah, that he heard him narrating from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed, the garments of the people of Paradise will shine with the pleasure of Allah, and a cloud will pass over them and call out to them: 'O people of Paradise, what do you wish that I rain upon you?' Until it rains upon them maidens of full bosom, of equal age."[[Also narrated by Abu Nu'aym in Tarikh Isbahan (1/195) through Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Sa'd, from Abu Sufyan Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Rabb ibn Taym al-Yashkuri, with this chain.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and a cup overflowing﴾, Ibn 'Abbas said: filled and continuous. Ikrimah said: pure. Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: ﴿dihaq﴾ means full and brimming. Mujahid [[In M: "Qatadah said."]] and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it means successive.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿they hear therein no idle talk nor lying﴾, it is like His saying: ﴿No idle talk therein nor any sinfulness﴾ [al-Tur: 23], meaning there is no vain speech devoid of benefit therein, nor sinful lying; rather it is the Abode of Peace, and everything in it is free from deficiency.
